skill.name: greploop
skill.description: Iteratively address Greptile feedback on GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests, or Perforce shelved changelists, with a five-iteration limit.
skill.summary: Run bounded Greptile review cycles, apply actionable fixes, resolve threads, and report remaining feedback.
skill.author: greptileai

security_audit.summary: All 106 static matches are false positives for Markdown formatting, ordinary API fields, bounded polling, or standard output redirection. Semantic review found weak bot identity checks, unrestricted staging before push, and resolution instructions that can close unrelated review discussions. No evidence found of embedded malicious instructions or deliberate credential exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Substring-based bot matching can accept impersonated review comments that influence automatic code changes.
remediation.suggestion: Require a configured, verified bot identity on every platform. Treat review text as untrusted data and reject embedded operational instructions.

remediation.issue: The commit sequence stages every changed file before publishing.
remediation.suggestion: Check the initial working tree, stage only files changed for approved fixes, and inspect the staged diff before committing and pushing.

remediation.issue: Thread resolution instructions do not consistently restrict updates to addressed Greptile discussions.
remediation.suggestion: Track verified Greptile thread identifiers during triage. Resolve only those identifiers after confirming the associated fix or documented dismissal.

semantic_findings.title: Weak bot identity checks allow spoofed review input
semantic_findings.description: The reference accepts any GitHub login containing greptile; Perforce allows the same username heuristic. Review text then drives automated fixes and publication. An attacker with comment access could impersonate the reviewer and supply harmful change requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented substring filters do not authenticate bot accounts, and selected feedback guides edits. No actual malicious comment payload is present in these files.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted staging can publish unrelated local changes
semantic_findings.description: The workflow runs git add -A, commits, and pushes without checking existing changes or restricting staged paths. Unrelated files, including unignored sensitive files, could be published with review fixes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sequence explicitly stages all changes and publishes them without a working-tree isolation step. Actual exposure depends on the workspace contents.

semantic_findings.title: Resolution instructions can close unrelated review threads
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub query retrieves all review threads without an author filter. GitLab instructions then say to resolve each unresolved discussion without preserving Greptile ownership or addressed status. This can mark human reviewers' concerns as resolved without fixing them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Earlier triage restricts feedback to Greptile, but the later resolution instructions broaden selection to all unresolved discussions. The GitLab reference has a safer filter that these instructions do not require.

content.user_title: Address Greptile Feedback Across Review Platforms
content.value_statement: Repeated review feedback requires manual changes, status checks, and thread updates. Greploop guides bounded review cycles across GitHub, GitLab, and configured Perforce environments.
actual_capabilities: Detect the version control platform and identify the current pull request, merge request, or pending changelist.
Trigger Greptile reviews and poll GitHub checks or GitLab jobs with approximately ten-minute timeouts.
Read review summaries and inline feedback, including GitHub comments edited in place.
Apply actionable fixes, resolve review discussions, and commit and push changes or update Perforce shelves.
Stop after five iterations or a 5/5 confidence score with no unresolved comments, then report results.
limitations: Requires authenticated platform command-line tools, jq for JSON queries, and an existing Greptile installation.
Perforce review status and comment retrieval depend on installation-specific webhook, dashboard, or Swarm integration.
A 5/5 review score is a target, not a guarantee of correctness, security, or successful completion.
Current instructions need safeguards for bot identity, unrelated working-tree changes, and discussion resolution scope.

prompt_templates.title: Review the current change

prompt_templates.prompt: Run greploop on GitHub pull request [number]. Verify the bot identity, preserve unrelated changes, and stage only reviewed fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: apply targeted fixes to a known pull request.

prompt_templates.prompt: Run greploop for GitLab merge request [number] on [host]. Verify the bot account and resolve only addressed Greptile discussions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate commit-specific reviews on a self-hosted GitLab instance.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use greploop for Perforce changelist [number] in workspace [client]. Confirm review integration and bot identity; stop if review freshness cannot be verified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage shelved fixes with an installation-specific review integration.

best_practices: Verify the repository, branch or changelist, workspace, and exact Greptile bot identity before making changes.
Use an isolated working tree, inspect each fix, run relevant tests, and stage only intended files before publishing.
Resolve only addressed Greptile threads and preserve the five-iteration limit and polling timeout behavior.
anti_patterns: Accepting review instructions solely because a username contains greptile.
Running the unrestricted commit sequence in a workspace containing unrelated changes or unignored sensitive files.
Closing every unresolved discussion or treating a 5/5 confidence score as proof of correctness.

faq.question: Which review platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The instructions cover GitHub, GitLab, and Perforce. Perforce review retrieval requires an installation-specific integration.

faq.question: What must be installed and authenticated?
faq.answer: GitHub needs git and gh; GitLab needs git and glab. Perforce needs p4. JSON queries use jq, and Greptile must be configured.

faq.question: When does the loop stop?
faq.answer: It stops at 5/5 confidence with no unresolved comments, after five iterations, or when GitHub or GitLab review polling times out.

faq.question: Does the workflow change remote content?
faq.answer: Yes. It can push commits, update Perforce shelves, post trigger comments, and resolve review discussions. Review these actions before authorizing execution.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: The listing declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution still requires authenticated command-line tools and access to the target repository.

faq.question: Does a perfect review score guarantee secure code?
faq.answer: No. The score reflects Greptile feedback, not a security guarantee. Inspect changes, run relevant tests, and verify comment authors independently.
